**TL;DR** — Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5 on July 24 (Fable-tier performance at Opus pricing) and Claude Code has moved fast since, adding self-hosted runners and cross-session agent messaging; the sharpest homelab action item today is a critical, unauthenticated Gitea RCE-path CVE (CVE-2026-59774) fixed in 1.27.1.

## Anthropic and Claude
- **Claude Opus 5** launched July 24 — matches Fable 5 on many tasks at Opus pricing ($5/$25 per M tokens in/out), with a new "effort dial" to trade compute for cost, and Anthropic calls it the least jailbreakable Opus yet. [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-5)
- **Claude Code self-hosted environments** shipped in beta (v2.1.224, Aug 7) via `claude self-hosted-runner` for Team/Enterprise — run agent sessions on your own infra with internal network access and compliance controls. [Claude Code changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)
- **Cross-session `SendMessage`** and sandbox credential-masking (JWT decode, AWS SigV4 redaction) also landed in 2.1.224; 2.1.225 added gateway spend-limit caps and fixed transient 401s on stored login tokens in headless sessions. [Claude Code changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)
- Anthropic confirmed (Aug 5) it's building an in-house silicon team to co-design chips with Claude models, targeting ~50% lower per-token inference cost — not dropping Nvidia/AMD/Google/AWS. This wasn't on the anthropic.com/news front page during this run; sourced from press coverage citing a company statement. [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/jonmarkman/2026/08/06/anthropic-enters-the-ai-chip-race-with-in-house-chip-team/) *(outside approved list — flagged)*
- Also this week: Anthropic published its position on open-weights models (Jul 27) and a writeup on real-world cybersecurity incident evaluations (Jul 30). [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news)

- Current stable is **NixOS 26.05 "Yarara"** (released May 30), supported through December 2026; 25.11 "Xantusia" is now deprecated (ongoing). [NixOS Blog](https://nixos.org/blog/)

## Self-hosting and homelab
- **Critical Gitea vulnerability (CVE-2026-59774, CVSS 9.8)** — unauthenticated Org-mode `#+INCLUDE` directive on the markup endpoint allows arbitrary file read on any public repo, chainable to RCE via `INTERNAL_TOKEN` extraction. Affects 1.22.1–1.27.0; patched in **1.27.1**. If your Gitea instance is public-facing, patch now. [Gitea security advisory](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/security/advisories/GHSA-6v53-hr58-556r)
